body:
Note that `RefCounted` objects exist only as long as they are referenced. Also, standard `Callable`s don't increment the reference count, while `call_deferred()` adds call arguments to the message queue as hard references.

So, the problem is in the object's lifetime. If you replace the local variable with a member variable, it will work as expected.

If you comment out lines 4 and 5 in the `_ready()` function body in your example, you'll notice that line 3 also doesn't output anything. It only works because line 4 is executed, which extends the object's lifetime.

If you want a `Callable` to keep a `RefCounted` object alive as long as it exists, you can wrap it in a lambda or use my `reference_callable()` wrapper (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/74990#issuecomment-3496982509). However, be careful, as this can lead to memory leaks in more complex cases.

Wow thank you! That totally explains the behavior I'm seeing, I had removed some caching somewhere in my project, and found that it broke the deferred call being made somewhere completely different - presumably because I'd gotten rid of the only reference to the object I was calling the method on.

It looks like the linked issue covers the issue of refcounted objects being freed even if their methods are referenced by a callable (which I think is exactly what is causing this behavior), and I can understand the risk of any fix for this being a breaking change.

What would it look like to update the logic under call_deferred to drop a warning if the callable's object has been freed? That way it's clearer in this kind of situation that something is going wrong, and the issue is related to object references.
Happy to have a go at contributing the update for this warning if it's something that makes sense to add

> What would it look like to update the logic under call_deferred to drop a warning if the callable's object has been freed?

On the one hand, this might seem like a good idea. But on the other, it can be inconvenient for those who explicitly rely on the current behavior, those who want all deferred calls to be automatically canceled when the instance is freed.

We had a similar issue with `await` (suspended coroutines). This is frustrating for users, as it leaves them no choice but to either not use this functionality (unless they are absolutely sure about the object lifetime) or put up with false positive errors/warnings cluttering the log.

That's fair enough, I wonder if there's a way to add the warning, as well as a way of making the call_deferred call that makes it clear that it's not an issue if the callback never fires. The first thing that comes to mind would be to add another function, e.g. call_deferred_if_alive, which doesn't throw the error, or to add an optional boolean argument to call_deferred like ok_if_freed, which causes it to not fire the warning.

If we really wanted to avoid disturbing any existing usage, we could also do the opposite, add a function which will throw a warning (or even an error) if the object is freed, e.g. call_deferred_or_fail.
Personally I feel that the existing behavior is unexpected enough that it's worth changing the default, but I can accept that I may be biased 😅 

I'm also conscious that this might be bloating the codebase too much over a minor issue, if it's not worth a fix I think that's probably fine, hopefully finding the issue can help people understand in the cases where it happens to them.
